answer: Yes. Each central character has distinctive traits and motivations beyond their plot function. Carl’s tedious lectures coexist with perceptiveness and fear of abandonment; Martin’s genuine kindness also conceals emotional disengagement; Lizzy has creative ambitions, illness, and morally complicated reasons for confessing; and Johan combines emotional resonance with compromised intimacy. The narrator’s self-deception and eventual self-understanding anchor these layered relationships. Their differing degrees of development suit their roles without making anyone feel merely functional.
